reasons: The two-point proposition is obsolete: the same regular witness supports an affine recession ray whose published-class identified set is all of \(\mathbb R\), while retaining the two bounded-class endpoint witnesses as the middle stage of the identification elbow.
The published completion class must be an explicit object before its identified set can be contrasted with the strengthened sensitivity-class interval.
The unbounded source-class conclusion requires an explicit legal completion for every finite real ray index.
A declared family of full-data laws is needed to attain every real source-class value.
The strengthened counterexample must distinguish the unrestricted published completion class from the bounded sensitivity class.
The recession ray uses one declared baseline-trend direction, equal to the positive bounded-class witness trend.
A free real index is needed to exhibit the full recession ray.
The construction correction introduces \(H\), \(f_{XZ}\), \(f_0\), \(P\), and \(R(P)\), so the complete definition metadata must be replaced atomically with the corrected construction.

correct: The old handle proposed a shrinking support hole inside a class whose fixed known rectangle support and uniform positive density lower bound rule out that construction. The corrected handle separates the admissible fixed-support \(R(P)\to0\) problem from a future varying-support problem and makes clear that constructing a valid least-favorable family remains the crux.

comparator-promise-table-replace: The 2024 proceedings singleton is disproved over its published class by an unbounded completion ray, whereas the positive interval belongs to a strengthened sensitivity class; this is non-representability, not strict tightening.
The narrowed open question names the fixed support \(H\) and the varying law \(P\), so its statement text and free-symbol metadata must move together; its dependencies remain unchanged.

narrow: The current question combines two regimes that the frozen class cannot contain. By \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) for the fixed known rectangle family \(\mathscr R\) and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on \(H\), every law in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) has the same support topology. Thus \(R(P)\to0\) is a legitimate fixed-support transition, whereas an approaching conditional-support hole requires a new varying-support class. The proposed wording narrows the open question to the regime represented by the existing primitives and explicitly separates the unsupported regime.

narrow: The existing comparative sentence incorrectly presents sharpness for the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz completion slice as an extension of the unrestricted published class. The corrected claim preserves the proved sharp equality but confines it to the declared sensitivity class, makes the simultaneous diagonal clause explicit, records that marginal quasi-stayers are unused, and disclaims transfer to the published-class identified set.
